steps.title: Prepare sensor and sample hardware
steps.instruction: Gather the plate lid, green sensor rack, sensor plate, rack base, and sample plate; use two 96‑well plates – one (sensor plate) for soaking streptavidin biosensors and one (sample plate) for the assay.

steps.title: Load sensors and buffer
steps.instruction: Place the required number of Octet® streptavidin (SA) biosensors into the green sensor rack; dispense 200 µL of BLI binding buffer into each well of the sensor plate that corresponds to a sensor position; keep the sensor rack and sensor plate separate while setting up the software.

steps.title: Prepare ligand and analyte solutions
steps.instruction: a) Dissolve the entire vial of powdered biotinylated RALF1 and RALF1‑KR in DMSO to obtain 11 mg/mL stock solutions, aliquot 20 µL into 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes and store at –20 °C; dilute each stock in BLI binding buffer to a working concentration of 5 µg/mL and keep on ice. b) Dissolve the entire vial of powdered OG25‑50 (DP 25‑50) in Milli‑Q water to obtain 10 mg/mL stock, aliquot 50 µL into 2.0 mL tubes and store at –20 °C; prepare analyte solutions in BLI binding buffer at 0, 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 µM and keep on ice.

steps.title: Assemble 96‑well assay plate
steps.instruction: Using a flat‑bottom black 96‑well plate, fill each well to a final volume of 200 µL as follows: column 1 – 200 µL BLI binding buffer (baseline buffer); column 2 – 200 µL of 5 µg/mL RALF1 or RALF1‑KR (loading ligand); column 3 – 200 µL BLI binding buffer (post‑loading baseline and dissociation); column 4 – 200 µL OG25‑50 solutions at the specified concentrations (0‑5 µM).

steps.title: Switch on instrument
steps.instruction: Turn on the Octet RED96 instrument about 40 min before the run to allow temperature equilibration.

steps.title: Define plate layout in software
steps.instruction: In the Octet Data Acquisition software open the Plate Definition tab, assign each column as Buffer (B), Loading/Ligand (L) or Sample/Analyte (S) using the right‑mouse button, and enter the Sample ID and concentration for every well so the software layout matches the physical plate prepared in the previous step.

steps.title: Create assay steps
steps.instruction: In the Assay Definition tab create the following steps in order: sensorcheck, Loading, Baseline, Association, Dissociation; set each of Loading, Baseline, Association and Dissociation to a duration of 600 s and keep the shake speed at the default 1000 rpm; assemble the steps into a workflow (sensorcheck → Loading → Baseline → Association → Dissociation) and assign the appropriate Sample column, Step Name, Step Type and Sensor Type.

steps.title: Assign sensors to wells
steps.instruction: In the Sensor Assignment tab highlight sensor positions A1–G1 in the sensor tray, right‑click to set Sensor Type to SA (streptavidin), remove any unused positions (e.g., H1), and verify that the number and arrangement of sensors correspond exactly to the layout prepared in Section A.

steps.title: Review experiment configuration
steps.instruction: In the Review Experiment tab confirm: (a) sensors are assigned to A1–G1 only; (b) plate definition matches the buffer, ligand and sample wells and their IDs/concentrations; (c) assay definition step order is sensorcheck → Loading → Baseline → Association → Dissociation.

steps.title: Run BLI measurement
steps.instruction: In the Run Experiment tab choose a data‑save directory, enter an experiment name and file prefix, verify run settings (plate temperature, shake mode, acquisition rate), stack the sensor rack (pre‑mounted sensors), sensor plate and rack base as shown in Figure 2, insert the stacked sensor hardware on the left side and the prepared sample plate on the right side of the Octet RED96, then press GO to start the measurement.

steps.title: Select raw data for analysis
steps.instruction: Launch the Octet Data Analysis software, navigate to the experiment folder in the Data Selection window and select the corresponding data file.

steps.title: Process sensorgrams
steps.instruction: a) Choose Raw Data View; b) Assign each sensor as Ligand or Reference; c) Activate Customize; d) In the Customize Sensor Subtraction window perform reference subtraction (Ligand – Reference); e) Enable Align Y Axis to set all curves to a common zero baseline; f) Select Align to Dissociation; g) Apply Savitzky‑Golay filtering; h) Inspect the processed traces; i) Save the processed sensorgrams with Save Raw Data; j) Click Process Data to move corrected curves to the Analysis tab.

steps.title: Set kinetic analysis parameters
steps.instruction: In the Analysis tab select Association and Dissociation under ‘Step to Analyze’, choose the 1:1 binding model, select Global (Full) fitting, set Rmax Unlinked By Sensor, verify that the Association and Dissociation windows span the full measurement period (default 0–600 s each).

steps.title: Fit curves and export results
steps.instruction: Click ‘Fit Curves!’ to generate kinetic fits, residuals and rate constants (k_on, k_off, K_D); then export the fitted results, including KD values, sensor‑specific fits, residual plots and fitting tables, using Save Report.

steps.title: Normalize data for GraphPad
steps.instruction: Perform the following calculations for each sensorgram: (a) Reference subtraction B_corr(t) = B_ligand(t) − B_ref(t); (b) Baseline normalization B_norm(t) = B_corr(t) − B_corr(t₀); (c) Time normalization t_corr = t − t₀; export the normalized data and import into GraphPad Prism for high‑resolution plotting.
